Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika Mandanna 's 'Ranabaali' crossed the Rs 50 cr mark in India net collections after recording an increase in earnings on its second Saturday. According to Sacnilk reports, the Telugu period drama collected Rs 2.80 cr on day 9 from 1,569 shows. This represents a 33.3% rise over Friday's earnings of Rs 2.10 cr. The film's cumulative India net collection has reached Rs 50.10 cr, while its domestic gross stands at Rs 58.25 cr. Overseas earnings have also contributed to its overall theatrical performance. Watch ‘Chalo-Chalo…Already late’, says Rashmika Mandanna as she gets papped at airport 'Ranabaali' world wide collections at Rs 70.10 cr
 The film earned Rs 40 lakhs in overseas gross collections on Saturday, taking its cumulative overseas total to Rs 11.85 cr. Its worldwide gross collection now stands at Rs 70.10 cr. The movie generated an average of Rs 17,846 per show during its ninth day in theatres. 'Ranabaali' opened with Rs 9.25 cr on October 16. It followed that performance with Rs 7.30 cr on Saturday and Rs 7.50 cr on Sunday. Monday's collection stood at Rs 5.40 cr, while Tuesday brought in Rs 7.10 cr. The film subsequently earned Rs 5.50 cr on Wednesday and Rs 3.15 cr on Thursday. Its first-week India net total reached Rs 45.20 cr. The movie collected Rs 2.10 cr on its second Friday before recording an improvement the following day.  The Telugu 2D version registered 34.58% overall occupancy on Saturday. Morning screenings recorded 24.15%, followed by 33.23% in the afternoon. Evening occupancy reached 35.77%, while night shows registered the highest figure at 41.15%. The film attracted 232,282 footfalls on Day 9, taking cumulative attendance to 4,001,524. The rise in Saturday's collections coincided with stronger occupancy compared with the previous day. Directed by Rahul Sankrityan, 'Ranabaali' unfolds against the backdrop of the Madras Famine of 1876–1878 in the Rayalaseema region. The story follows a horseman who leads a local uprising against British colonial rule. Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika Mandanna play the lead roles, while Arnold Vosloo is also part of the cast.
